title: Projectile motion
competency: Describe horizontal and inclined projectile motion and solve problems on time of flight, range and maximum height.

keywords.def: An object in flight that moves only under gravity after it is thrown or launched.
The path a projectile follows. Without air resistance it is a parabola.
The angle θ between the launch velocity and the horizontal.
The time a projectile spends in the air.
The horizontal distance a projectile covers before it lands at launch level.
The greatest height above the launch level, reached when the vertical velocity is zero.

en.text: A projectile moves under gravity only. Its horizontal velocity stays constant; vertically it falls with acceleration g. A body thrown horizontally from height h lands after t = √(2h/g), the same time as a body dropped from rest, and travels Δx = v₀t.

am.text: ተወንጫፊ በስበት ብቻ ይንቀሳቀሳል። አግድም ፍጥነቱ አይለወጥም፤ ቁልቁል በ g ይወድቃል። ከ h ከፍታ በአግድም የተወረወረ ነገር በ t = √(2h/g) ያርፋል።

screens.title: Dropped or thrown?
screens.ask: From the same height, Abebe drops one stone and throws another straight out sideways at the same moment. Which lands first?
opts: It depends on the stones' mass
screens.after: They land together. Gravity pulls both down the same way; sideways speed does not change the fall.

screens.title: What is a projectile?
paras: A projectile is thrown or launched, then moves under gravity only.
A kicked football, a bullet and a jet of water are projectiles.
We assume: g = 9.8 m/s², always downward.
We ignore air resistance.
So the horizontal velocity stays constant.
The horizontal and vertical motions are independent. They share the same time t.
The path, or trajectory, is a parabola.

screens.title: Horizontal projection
paras: The body leaves with horizontal velocity v₀ and no vertical velocity.
Down is taken as positive here.
screens.note: Time of flight from height h: t = √(2h/g). Range: R = v₀√(2h/g).

screens.title: Throw from a cliff
screens.ask: Change the height and the launch speed. Watch the landing distance.
screens.note: The time of flight depends only on h.

screens.title: Key words
defs: An object in flight that moves only under gravity after it is thrown or launched.
The path a projectile follows. Without air resistance it is a parabola.

screens.text: A rescue plane flies level and drops a food package. Ignoring air, where is the plane when the package lands?
screens.why: The package keeps the plane's horizontal velocity, so they stay in line.
screens.clue: What happens to the horizontal velocity of the package?

screens.ask: A package is dropped from a plane 300 m high. g = 10 m/s². It reaches the ground after ≈ ___ s (2 decimal places)
screens.why: t = √(2 × 300/10) = √60 = 7.75 s. (The book truncates to 7.74 s.)
screens.clue: Use h = ½gt² with no starting vertical velocity.

screens.ask: The plane flies at 360 km/h. It must release the package ≈ ___ m before it is over the driver (nearest metre)
screens.clue: Change km/h to m/s first, then use Δx = v₀t.

screens.ask: A ball is thrown horizontally at 20 m/s from a building 90 m high. g = 10 m/s². Time of flight ≈ ___ s (2 decimal places)
screens.clue: Only the height decides the time.

screens.ask: Same ball: it lands ≈ ___ m from the foot of the building (nearest metre)
screens.clue: Horizontal speed stays 20 m/s.

screens.ask: Same ball: it hits the ground at ≈ ___ m/s (1 decimal place)
screens.clue: Combine vₓ and v_y with Pythagoras.

screens.ask: A gun with muzzle speed 500 m/s aims at a target 50 m away. g = 10 m/s². To hit it, aim ≈ ___ cm above the target
screens.clue: Find the time to reach the target first.

en.text: A body launched at angle θ has v₀ₓ = v₀cosθ and v₀y = v₀sinθ. The horizontal velocity stays v₀cosθ. Vertically v_y = v₀sinθ − gt, so it rises, stops rising at the top and falls back. Time to the top is v₀sinθ/g; over level ground the time of flight is 2v₀sinθ/g.

am.text: በማዕዘን θ የተወረወረ ነገር v₀cosθ አግድም፣ v₀sinθ ቁልቁል ፍጥነት አለው። ከፍተኛ ቦታ ላይ v_y = 0 ነው። የበረራ ጊዜ 2v₀sinθ/g ነው።

screens.title: At the very top
screens.ask: A football is kicked up at an angle. At the highest point of its path, what is true?
screens.after: At the top only the vertical velocity is zero. The ball still moves sideways, and gravity still pulls down.

screens.title: Launching at an angle
paras: Split the launch velocity into two parts.
Horizontal: v₀ₓ = v₀cosθ. It never changes.
Vertical: v₀y = v₀sinθ. Gravity slows it, then reverses it.
screens.note: The book writes +gt and +½gt² with g = −9.8 m/s². Both forms give the same answers.

screens.title: Time of flight
paras: At the top v_y = 0, so the time to the top is t = v₀sinθ/g.
Over level ground the fall takes the same time.
Time of flight: T = 2v₀sinθ/g.
Use T only when launch and landing are at the same level.

screens.title: A ball kicked toward a wall
steps: v₀ = 25 m/s at 53°, wall 24 m away, g = 10 m/s², cos53° = 0.6, sin53° = 0.8.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The angle θ between the launch velocity and the horizontal.
The time a projectile spends in the air.

screens.text: At which point in an inclined flight is the speed least?
screens.why: There v_y = 0, so only vₓ is left.
screens.clue: Which part of the velocity disappears at the top?

screens.text: At the highest point the velocity and the acceleration are perpendicular.
screens.why: The velocity is horizontal there and g points straight down.
screens.clue: Which way does each point at the top?

screens.ask: A body launched at 30 m/s reaches its highest point after 1.5 s. g = 10 m/s². The launch angle is ___°
screens.why: v₀sinθ = gt = 15, so sinθ = 15/30 = 0.5 and θ = 30°.
screens.clue: At the top v_y = 0: v₀sinθ = gt.

screens.ask: Same body: its range is ≈ ___ m (1 decimal place)
screens.clue: Total time is twice the time to the top.

screens.text: Which are true for a projectile (no air resistance)?
pool: Its acceleration is g downward everywhere
Its vertical velocity is zero at the top
Its acceleration is zero at the top
a: Its acceleration is g downward everywhere
Its vertical velocity is zero at the top
screens.why: Gravity never switches off, so the acceleration is never zero.
screens.clue: Think about what gravity does at the top.

screens.ask: A projectile's launch speed is five times its speed at the top. The launch angle is ≈ ___° (1 decimal place)
screens.why: At the top speed = v₀cosθ. v₀ = 5v₀cosθ gives cosθ = 0.2, θ = 78.5°.
screens.clue: What speed is left at the top?

en.text: Over level ground the range is R = v₀² sin2θ/g and the maximum height is H = v₀² sin²θ/(2g). The range is greatest at 45°, and complementary angles such as 30° and 60° give the same range. A steeper launch always gives a greater height.

am.text: አግድም ርቀት R = v₀² sin2θ/g፣ ከፍተኛ ከፍታ H = v₀² sin²θ/(2g) ነው። በ45° ርቀቱ ትልቁ ነው፤ ተደጋጋፊ ማዕዘኖች እኩል ርቀት ይሰጣሉ።

screens.title: Aim the kick
screens.ask: Change the speed and the angle. Find the angle with the longest range. Compare 30° with 60°.

screens.title: Range and height formulas
paras: Range: R = v₀² sin2θ/g.
The greatest range is at θ = 45°: R_max = v₀²/g.
Angles that add to 90° give the same range.
Maximum height: H = v₀² sin²θ/(2g).
Linking them: H = R tanθ/4.
These need launch and landing at the same level.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The horizontal distance a projectile covers before it lands at launch level.
The greatest height above the launch level, reached when the vertical velocity is zero.

screens.text: Which launch angle gives the greatest range over level ground?
screens.why: sin2θ is largest (1) when 2θ = 90°.
screens.clue: When is sin2θ biggest?

screens.text: Balls A (37°) and B (53°) are kicked with the same speed. Which statement is true?
opts: B goes farther; A goes higher
screens.why: 37° + 53° = 90°, so sin2θ is equal. The steeper ball rises higher.
screens.clue: Add the two angles.

screens.ask: A ball is kicked at 40 m/s at 37°. g = 10 m/s², sin37° = 0.6. Maximum height H = ___ m
screens.clue: Square sin37° before you multiply.

screens.ask: Same kick, sin74° = 0.96. Range R ≈ ___ m (nearest metre)
screens.clue: Use sin2θ, not sinθ.

screens.text: The range of a projectile is 3 times its maximum height. The launch angle is about
screens.why: H = R tanθ/4, so tanθ = 4H/R = 4/3 and θ ≈ 53°.
screens.clue: Use H = R tanθ/4.

screens.text: The same launch is made on the Moon (g ≈ 1.6 m/s²). Compared with Earth, the range is
screens.why: R ∝ 1/g and 9.8 ÷ 1.6 ≈ 6. The height is also about 6 times greater.
screens.clue: g is in the denominator.

screens.ask: A long jumper leaves the ground at 11.0 m/s and 20.0° (sin40° = 0.643). g = 10 m/s². Jump length ≈ ___ m (1 decimal place)
screens.clue: Treat the jump as level ground: R = v₀² sin2θ/g.

items.text: A gun with muzzle speed 500 m/s shoots at a target 50 m away. To hit it, the gun should be aimed
items.why: The bullet drops ½ × 10 × 0.1² = 0.05 m in 0.1 s.
items.clue: How far does the bullet fall on the way?

items.ask: A long jumper (11.0 m/s, 20.0°, g = 10 m/s², sin20° = 0.342) rises ≈ ___ m (2 decimal places)

test.ask: A stone is thrown horizontally at 15 m/s from a 20 m cliff. g = 10 m/s². It lands after ___ s
Same stone: it lands ___ m from the foot of the cliff

test.text: Which angle gives the same range as 30° for the same speed?

A ball is kicked at 20 m/s at 30°. g = 10 m/s². Maximum height H = ___ m

notes.text: Example 2.1: t = √0.004 = 0.0632 s; using it gives v₀ ≈ 474 m/s, not 500 m/s (the book rounds t to 0.06 s too early).
Example 2.2: √60 = 7.746 s ≈ 7.75 s and Δx ≈ 775 m (book truncates to 7.74 s, 774 m). The package must be released 774–775 m BEFORE the driver.
Example 2.3: denominator printed as 10 m/s; should be 10 m/s². R = 153.6 m with sin74° = 0.96 or 153.8 m with 0.961.
Sign of g: the book writes v_y = v₀sinθ + gt and Δy = v₀sinθ t + ½gt² with g = −9.8 m/s². Lessons use up-positive with −gt and −½gt² (g = +9.8). Teachers should point out both forms.
Exercise 2.1 Q3 and Q4 answers use g = 10 m/s² (Q4 with 9.8 gives R ≈ 7.94 m, H ≈ 0.722 m). The questions state g = 10 m/s².
Activities 2.1–2.4 (table-top launches) are hands-on and are not turned into graded items.
